counts.externalElementsNote: 820 external physical space boundaries exist and none resolved: swept curve is not a readable polyline. The classifier reads IfcSurfaceOfLinearExtrusion (Revit); this file's boundaries are another surface type. Envelope areas here come from the wall walk, not from boundaries, so nothing published depends on this.

areas.openingsNote: Glazing aperture 106.06 m² = 51 IfcWindow at OverallWidth × OverallHeight (106.06 m²). Exterior doors are separate — a door is aperture, not glazing: 16 IfcDoor, 81.03 m², OverallWidth × OverallHeight. Host wall by IfcRelFillsElement → IfcOpeningElement → IfcRelVoidsElement (0 openings), or where that chain does not reach the exterior-wall set, by an exterior wall adjacent in the opening's plane within 0.3 m (67). Sector is the host wall's, from the same orientation pass as the wall split. Envelope by a both-sides probe against the conditioned IfcSpace solids (6 of 100 have geometry, so an empty probe is inconclusive and the host wall decides); this file has no IfcCurtainWall; 5 openings hosted in walls outside the exterior set; 12 window(s) (19.49 m²) and 81 door(s) (201.7 m²) sit in the plane of walls outside the exterior-wall set and are not counted — the wall names are on each row; 247 sub-frames; 52 unresolved (11.9 m² where a size is stated). IsExternal is reported per row and never used as a filter — it means "not an interior partition" to an authoring tool, never "bounds conditioned space against outdoor air". It marks 20 door(s) here; 16 confirm against an exterior wall, 4 do not: #77756 merk F-R 4.23 m², #81462 merk F-R 4.23 m², #187290 merk F-R 4.23 m², #189383 merk F-R 4.23 m². Rows in openings.json.
areas.volumeNote: Gross from 100 spaces (floor area × storey height; voids, and rooms taller than their storey with no void above, as their own solids); net from 100 spaces (100 from stated volume quantity). A closed tessellation's signed volume is exact.
areas.roofNote: Plan shadow per element (union of its projected triangles, ifc-plan-shadow.mjs): 78 elements — 62 IfcSlab.PredefinedType=ROOF, 16 by declared slab name (dakvloer, plat dak, lifttop). roofProjectedSqm sums 10 roof type(s), each as the union of its elements; the elements themselves sum to 519.27 m² (elements of one type overlapping in plan) and all types together cover 361.86 m² (one type above another). surfaceSqm is each element's true one-sheet surface (Σ area of its upward faces; ÷ 2 where a surface model has no downward face and both sheets are wound upward; ÷ the coverage where its parts cover its shadow more than once, as stacked layer solids do — surfaceBasis says which), summing to 692.04 m²; a flat deck's surface equals its shadow, a pitched roof's exceeds it. 34 element(s) present their top face more than once (upward-face sum above shadow) — the reason the shadow is used and Σ area×n_y is not. 1 shadow(s) needed a vertex grid coarser than 1 µm to union. The file types its flat roof decks as IfcSlab FLOOR — dakvloer (9 slabs at 11.62–11.84 m on storey '04 dak'), plat dak (6 at 5.67–5.84 m, the low-rise wing) and lifttop (1 at 12.60–12.80 m) — so they are declared roof by name; a type-only rule found 136 m² of roof on a four-storey block. gootconstructie (gutters), prefab balkon (balconies) and the FLOOR-typed dakisolatie stacked on the lifttop are not declared. The pitched sporenkap is exported as stacked layer solids, which is why its upward-face sum exceeds its shadow.
areas.groundNote: IfcSlab (not ROOF or LANDING) on storeys at or below 00 begane grond (0 m): 81 candidate(s). A slab counts as ground envelope when a conditioned space stands on it — its shadow overlaps a conditioned ground-storey space footprint (32 of 32 such spaces have one: 3 solid, 29 footprint) or an IfcRelSpaceBoundary names it as bounding one. IsExternal is not consulted. 81 counted, 0 excluded. groundSlabSqm is the union of the counted shadows (they sum to 678.28 m²; stacked build-up layers count once); groundPerimeterM is the outline's outer ring; 2 hole ring(s) totalling 4.06 m are reported and not added.

orientation.note: Azimuths are clockwise from north, where north is the model's -Z after web-ifc's Z-up to Y-up conversion. Outward face inferred by comparing each face's centroid with the building centre, which is correct for a convex plan and can be wrong at a re-entrant corner. All 122 inner-leaf walls are cardinal; the diagonal sectors are 0 by measurement. The model's 88 placements at 47.94° are the excluded outer leaf (buitenblad), so no envelope area is mis-binned.

site.locationNote: IfcSite states 52°9'N 5°23'E — a whole-minute value with zero seconds, 46.2 km from the real Schependomlaan in Nijmegen and in Amersfoort, the authoring architect's own city. It is a stamped constant, not a survey: no position, orientation or solar geometry may be taken from it. The town 'Nijmegen' IS stated, on both IfcSite and IfcBuilding, and is the only spatial fact this model supports. TrueNorth is the schema default (0.,1.) in both representation contexts, so orientation is an assumption — and note the geometry is not purely cardinal: 88 element placements sit at 47.94°.

model.note: Building fabric from the architectural model only: walls, slabs, stairs, glazing, doors and mullions. Nothing from the subcontractor models is in this file — the steel frame, precast floors, roof tiling, railings and blockwork are their own layers.
model.serviceNote: Six layers from the 33 subcontractor models in the archive's coordination set (BIMsight Projectdata1). Five carry each supplier's geometry as modelled — a shape placed twice or more is stored once and instanced, everything else is merged. Every file declares millimetres and no distribution port, so no layer animates flow. The utilities layer is the exception and says so under its row: its 42 SketchUp objects are drawn as boxes.
